property_summary: If withdrawAll is called by the contract owner then the call must revert whenever the contract has zero balance; otherwise it must not revert.
If withdrawAll is called (by this test invoking it as owner) then it must revert exactly when the contract C's balance is zero, and must not revert when C's balance is nonzero.
If withdrawAll is called (by this test invoking it as owner) then it must revert exactly when the contract C's balance is zero, and must not revert when C's balance is nonzero.
If withdrawAll is called by the owner then it reverts exactly when C's balance is zero and does not revert when C's balance is nonzero.

After owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance is transferred to the specified recipient address (so address(c).balance becomes zero and address(recipient) increases by that amount), not to the caller.
For any caller, calling withdrawAll should not revert when msg.sender equals C.owner and should revert otherwise.
When withdrawAll is called by the contract owner it must not revert and the contract's balance must become zero (funds leave the contract).

If the caller is the owner, withdrawAll must succeed (not revert) and the caller's address must not receive the contract balance as a direct result of the call (i.e., address(this) balance becomes zero but address(this) of tester does not increase), so a successful call by owner never sends the contract balance to msg.sender.

When the owner calls withdrawAll with any recipient, the call should succeed (not revert) and exactly the provided recipient — not necessarily the caller — receives the contract's funds, so the call does not revert for owner callers.

For any caller equal to owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers the contract's entire balance to the provided recipient (so after call, address(c).balance == 0 and recipient's balance increased by previous balance); the mutant that sends funds to msg.sender violates this when owner != recipient.

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, after calling withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance becomes 0 (funds are forwarded to the supplied recipient); the mutant that sends funds to msg.sender instead of _recipient will violate this when owner != recipient because the supplied recipient won't receive the funds and address(c).balance may still become 0 but the intended recipient's balance won't increase — so we check that the supplied recipient receives the funds by observing address(c).balance == 0 and that the recipient's balance increased by the prior contract balance (the mutant breaks this when owner != recipient).
After withdrawAll is called by the owner, the contract's balance becomes zero and the recipient's balance increases by that amount (i.e., all funds are forwarded to the provided recipient).
If withdrawAll is called by the owner it must not revert (owner can successfully withdraw regardless of the provided recipient).
If withdrawAll(msg.sender) is called, then the call reverts exactly when msg.sender is not equal to c.owner().
withdrawAll reverts for callers who are not the contract owner (i.e., only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll).
withdrawAll should revert for non-owners and succeed for the owner (i.e., reverted == (msg.sender != c.owner())).

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers the contract's full balance to the provided recipient (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and the recipient's balance increases); the mutant that always pays owner breaks this because when owner calls with a recipient != owner the recipient does not receive the funds and address(c).balance may still become 0 but the recipient's balance does not increase.

For any caller equal to owner and any recipient address, after withdrawAll(recipient) the recipient's balance increases by the contract balance (i.e., recipient receives the funds); the mutant that always sends to owner violates this when recipient != owner.

For any caller equal to owner and any recipient address, after withdrawAll(recipient) the contract balance becomes 0 (the full balance is forwarded out); the mutant can still zero the contract but may not send funds to the provided recipient in some cases — however asserting address(c).balance == 0 holds for the reference for all inputs and is violated by the mutant when transferring to a recipient whose fallback reverts causing the mutant's transfer to owner to behave differently than the intended recipient transfer.

For any caller equal to owner and any recipient contract that reverts on receive, withdrawAll(recipient) in the reference either successfully forwards the full balance to that recipient (and returns ok=true) or the call reverts; the mutant that always pays owner can succeed (ok=true) while the reference would have reverted when the recipient reverts, so the behaviors differ.

For any owner caller and any recipient contract that rejects payments (reverts in receive/fallback), calling withdrawAll(recipient) must revert (so the call does not succeed) because the reference attempts to transfer to the provided recipient; the mutant that always transfers to owner can succeed when owner can receive funds, thus violating this property for some inputs.
